SMTO-CFG-0034 — SMTO's settings file uses a format it no longer supports

GUID: 1d283a6a-1162-4c43-84dc-e9e5da1de88a
Slug: config-config-version-is-no-longer-supported-supported
Domain: CFG · Subsystem: cfg

What happened

  • The startup settings file (usually config.yaml) says it uses an older format than this SMTO accepts, so SMTO stopped before starting. The file wasn't changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Make a copy of the settings file (usually config.yaml) before anyone edits it, and keep it somewhere safe. If the update goes wrong, you can still get back every setting the file held.
  2. Ask the person who manages SMTO to compare the config_version line with the supported range shown in the message, and rewrite the file in the current format. This SMTO only reads settings files whose format number falls in that range.
  3. Start SMTO again once the file is updated. SMTO reads this settings file only while it starts.

What success looks like

  • SMTO starts and the startup screen reaches Ready.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details (or copy the message from the window where SMTO was started) and send it to the person who manages SMTO. Don't delete the settings file to make SMTO start; you would lose the settings it holds.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Bootstrap configuration validation failed because config_version in the application YAML is below APP_CONFIG_MIN_SUPPORTED_VERSION after normalization.

What this means

  • Application config_version is below APP_CONFIG_MIN_SUPPORTED_VERSION after normalization. Validation reports the owning configuration boundary; it does not change settings, migrate retained state or grant authority. Existing tasks retain their accepted snapshots unless the specific control explicitly supports a live change.

Why this can happen

  • Application config_version is below APP_CONFIG_MIN_SUPPORTED_VERSION after normalization.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the actual saved version with the build's minimum and available supported migration path.

How to fix it

  • Preserve the original file, then inspect config_version in the file selected by --config, AOR_APP_CONFIG_PATH or config.yaml. With APP_CONFIG_MIN_SUPPORTED_VERSION = 1, a blank or 0 value normalizes to the current version, so only negative values reach this check; bring the sections in line with the current schema (or use the build that wrote the file) before setting a supported version, and validate with aor doctor --config.
  • Preserve the original configuration and use a supported migration or matching compatible build.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • A preserved, properly migrated compatible configuration validates.

What not to do

  • Do not remove retained state or weaken trust checks to make an unavailable dependency appear healthy.

Technical notes

  • Validation reports the owning configuration boundary; it does not change settings, migrate retained state or grant authority. Existing tasks retain their accepted snapshots unless the specific control explicitly supports a live change.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
